description: The bar chart, presented at an oblique angle, compares two methods — “Ours” and “Standard” — across three response categories: “Text,” “Generated Response,” and “Other,” as indicated by the legend at the bottom. The horizontal axis represents the percentage contribution of each category, while the vertical axis lists the two methods. For the “Ours” method, the blue “Text” segment accounts for 60.6%, the orange “Generated Response” segment for 31.7%, and the green “Other” segment for the remaining portion (approximately 7.7%, though not explicitly labeled). For the “Standard” method, the blue “Text” segment is 23.6%, the orange “Generated Response” segment is 51.1%, and the green “Other” segment is 25.3%. The chart visually emphasizes that “Ours” relies more heavily on “Text” responses, while “Standard” favors “Generated Response,” with “Other” being significantly higher under “Standard.” The bars are stacked horizontally, with each segment’s percentage labeled inside its respective colored block. The chart appears to illustrate the distribution of response types under each method, likely in the context of evaluating grounding supervision in natural language generation as suggested by the paper title.
